answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, so a voter’s influence depends on paths from trusted seeds rather than self-asserted identities. If a sybil cluster S has low conductance, φ(S)=cut(S,¬S)/vol(S), only a small fraction of walk probability escapes it per step; thus its aggregate voting weight is bounded by seed mass entering S plus leakage over the walk horizon. The jetty, reef, and ivory labels do not alter this min-cut bound.
